evals.prompt: docs-update architecture — we just split the monolith into 3 services (auth, billing, notifications), can you sync docs/architecture.md?
assertions: Reads the full existing docs/architecture.md and greps the codebase to verify the claimed service names/counts before writing, rather than trusting the old doc text
Runs a freshness check using docs/architecture.md's own git history (the resolved path from the argument), not a different or hardcoded document
Before filling any {{PLACEHOLDER}} tokens, determines which tokens the architecture template actually contains (e.g. via grep) rather than assuming a fixed list
Preserves any custom/manually-written sections in docs/architecture.md that aren't part of the template structure
Final report states the verified service count/names as facts traceable to a command run this session, not vague language like 'several services'

evals.prompt: docs-update all — sync everything with the current codebase, we've made a bunch of changes over the last month
assertions: Resolves scope to every doc currently present in docs/ and processes each one (concurrently via one subagent per doc if a Task tool is available, otherwise sequentially)
For at least one document, verifies claims against the codebase via grep/find rather than assuming the existing text is correct

When a specific claim in a document cannot be confirmed in the codebase (e.g. an SSO/auth claim with no matching code), removes or flags it instead of leaving it unverified or inventing supporting detail
Final report distinguishes updated docs from up-to-date/skipped docs, and does not claim a doc was 'updated' if nothing in it actually changed
Does not overwrite sections identified as custom/manual content

evals.prompt: docs-update security — update our security documentation (docs/security.md does not exist in this repo)
assertions: Recognizes docs/security.md does not currently exist rather than silently treating the request as a from-scratch creation
Does not write or create a new docs/security.md file with fabricated content
No mutating Write/Edit command is run against docs/security.md during this run
Final message tells the user to use docs-init (or equivalent) to create the document first, and stops there rather than generating one anyway
